harness.name: stwo-perf
harness.anchor_note: Native anchors were frozen on 2026-07-20 and RISC-V anchors on 2026-07-21 on the designated Apple M5 Max judge host (arm64 macOS, 18 CPU cores). Immutable reports live under autoresearch/reference/. Drift budgets are host-local and active.

workload_registry.note: Command templates are data so flag drift is a manifest edit, not a code change. The runner prepends the built bench binary of the owning group; {warmups}/{samples} come from the workload class sampling policy.
workload_registry.schema_note: Registry v2 (manifest_version bumped 1 -> 2): workloads live in named groups, each carrying one exclusively owned board plus its own build_step, binary, report_schema, and enabled flag. The registry now also owns the ordered workload classes plus their scoring, resource, timeout, and sampling policy; no consumer carries a parallel class enum. v1's flat build_step/binary/workloads triple is exactly today's group 'native'; loaders reject the flat shape with a migration hint. Disabled groups are announced loudly by every runner entry point, never silently dropped.

cuda.disabled_reason: core_cuda is staged only: all six Native AIR families are required, but only wide Fibonacci is exact and release-ready; exact family semantics, the stwo-perf CUDA report adapter, locked-host A/A calibration, pinned Rust verification, and complete structural coverage are not yet release-gated.

cairo_cpu.promotion_blocked_reason: TRACKS §7: cairo_cpu records evidence but cannot promote until per-(board, class) A/A dispersion and anchors are measured on the designated Apple M5 Max judge host and frozen into harness.anchor_* plus a cairo calibration freeze for board cairo_cpu. No Cairo calibration exists yet, so promotion fails closed; the gate opens only after that M5 calibration is committed.

acceptance_corpus.note: TRACKS §3.3 acceptance corpus: the pinned zksecurity/zkvm-benchmarks program matrix with expected cycle rules. Acceptance only — never a scored basket.

gates_policy.note: The Cairo product CLI proves exactly one statement per process, so one sample is one cold process; the runner owns the warmup/sample loop. Warmups must stay at or above one because the mandatory phase profile is recorded on a discarded warmup so scored samples run uninstrumented.

workload_provisioning.note: TRACKS §3.3 campaign portfolio entries whose prover inputs are host-local and far above the repository fixture budget. They are declared here so the basket's incompleteness is loud, never silent; generation commands live in autoresearch/schema/cairo-proof-v1.md. Entries here are not runnable workloads and are never scored.

The product descriptor in build_support/products/cairo_metal.zig still carries state .parity_gated behind its test-cairo-metal-product and test-cairo-metal-oracle release gates, no Metal-lane Cairo calibration exists on the designated judge host, and the generalized per-board Metal calibration (TRACKS §7) is not yet built. The group stays dark and fails closed.
cairo_metal.promotion_blocked_reason: TRACKS §7: no cairo_metal calibration exists on the designated Apple M5 Max judge host, and the product is parity_gated rather than released.

gates_policy.note: Mirrors cairo_cpu: one proof per cold process, phase profile recorded on a discarded warmup.

pr6_supremacy.disabled_reason: PR6 Supremacy remains disabled until every exact workload port, log22 oracle vector, both timing boundaries, locked-M5 statistical gate, and authenticated judged verdict are complete.

guards.note: The full native AIR portfolio plus the small wide-Fibonacci latency canary as mandatory regression guards: one declared objective workload is scored, but every selected guard's paired upper confidence bound must stay below its regression budget. Guards use the objective group's binary; args are data.

policy.note: pass = paired upper CI bound <= budget_upper; an inconclusive guard (CI straddling the budget after min rounds) samples inconclusive_extra_rounds more, then fails closed

impact_map.note: Editable-path prefixes to the guard sets a diff must exercise; generic prover/PCS/FFT/accumulation code touches every native AIR. Unmatched editable paths select every guard (fail closed).

holdout_generator.note: Judged runs draw one extra hold-out per class by jittering log_n_rows/sequence_len within class bounds; seed is recorded in the ledger row. Results publish as pass/fail only.

gates_policy.neutral_band_note: Promotion requires the declared-objective CI entirely below 1 - theta, where theta = max(theta_floor, dispersion_multiplier x per-class A/A dispersion recorded in the ledger epoch).

T0.note: correctness smoke plus ONE stage-profiled sample on the proxy fixture; the claimed phase must move here before T1 is scheduled. One warmup is the floor, not a nicety: the Cairo arm records its mandatory phase profile on a discarded warmup, so warmups=0 would leave that track with no phase evidence at all.

T1.note: paired ABBA on proxy fixtures with sequential early stopping and the PoW-excluded boundary; never ranks.

T2.note: full dual-boundary paired run on the contributor host, real classes, guards impact-mapped; the claimed verdict.

T3.note: judge-scheduled re-run plus audits on the designated host; the scored row. No cost target — the judge never trades honesty for time.

confirmation_ladder.note: TRACKS §3.5/§3.6. sequential_stop.enabled arms the pre-registered spending rule on scored paired runs; the T1 iterate path arms it explicitly because T1 never ranks. Absent this block the runner keeps pre-ladder fixed min/max-round behavior. Tier cost targets are CI-checked per track by scripts/check_tier_cost_targets.py.

qualification_policy.note: Fork CI is a cost-shifting qualification signal, never the trust root. Intake recomputes tree evidence and the central judge rebuilds and benchmarks hidden holdouts before promotion.
